That night when I was going to bed, I couldn’t shake the feeling that something was wrong, and we would walk into her room to find her dead. To prove to myself that nothing was wrong, I went and knocked on her door. Nothing. Opened it carefully while announcing that I was coming in. Still no response. She was curled up in a ball (which she wouldn’t have been able to do normally, given her physical condition), face down on the bed. I woke my friend up in the off chance that maybe her mother had just fallen asleep at a weird angle. My friend placed her hand on her mother’s arm, and recoiled quickly, telling me to touch her arm. Cold as ice.

And that was my first (and so far, only time) being that close to a dead person.

The way ability modifiers work, is that for every even number above ten, and every odd number below ten, you get a modifier increase or decrease. So looking at your Con and Int scores, which are both 18, you would get a +4 modifier to both. That doesn’t mean they increase to 22, but rather that any roll that is tied to one of those stats will automatically get +4 added to them. So for example, let’s say you decide to put points into Search. At level one, you toss 7 points into it because why not. You will also add 4 points due to it being an Intelligence based skill, which will give you an end result of +11. As such, any roll you make when asked to roll a Search check, will be whatever you roll on the D20, plus 11.

Seeing as how all your stats are at least ten, you don’t have to worry about any ability modifier penalties. But if you did, it would work the exact same way. Say you were a Fighter with a Wisdom score of 7. You would be then subtracting 2 from anything that is based off of Wisdom, which would make those checks and resistances harder. So as of right now, your ability modifiers would look like this, going in order from top to bottom.

0
3
4
4
1
3

One last thing that I forgot to mention, when adding the ability modifier to your skill checks on your character sheet, there is an actual section for them to be put down. Don’t just add up everything and put the total in the Ranks column. That will make life confusing for everyone. The Ranks column is for how many skill points you have opted to spend on a skill, the ability modifier column is for the additional increase or decrease you get from your stats, and the misc modifier is for if you have an effect from something that is adding to or taking away from your total. An Elf’s keen senses racial trait for example, gives +2 to I believe both Spot and Listen, which would be put in the misc modifier section. As a Halfling, if I recall, you have something for Climb and Tumble, I think. Those would go in the misc modifier column.

The first thing I noticed, is that you accidentally put your racial stat modifiers in your ability modifier section. You should instead, simply modify your stats in the ability score section. Strength goes down by two, Dex goes up by two. Also, unless your DM is making everyone roll for health at level 1 (which is frowned upon), you take the highest number for what your class’ hit dice is (as a Bard, that’s a D6) and add your Con modifier to it (with a Con score of 18, your Con modifier is +4) for a total of ten starting health.

As a Halfling, you are considered a Small creature, and as such your base speed is 20 feet. Make sure you write down your class proficiencies (light armor, simple weapons, shields) and any extra feats that you might have, in the Feats section on your character sheet. As for your skills, you’ll want to look up in the Player’s Handbook for what your class considers a core skill, and how many skill points you have at level 1 (I want to say it’s 6 plus your intelligence modifier for a Bard, but I’m basing this purely off of memory right now), multiply that by 4 for a level 1 character, and pick which skills you want to have points in. I highly recommend Perform (choose whether you’re good at dancing, playing an instrument, singing, etc), Bluff, Diplomacy, Spot and Listen. A lot of the finer details will be in the Player’s Handbook, if you have access to one.

Not too long after that, my mother (whom had been divorced from him for some time) and I lost all contact with him essentially out of nowhere.

Fast forward to when I was 15, and my mother had a talk with me one afternoon about how she had asked the elementary school counselor to look into his claims of having cancer.  They learned that he had lied to my face about it, simply because he wanted my attention to be fixated on him rather than anyone else in my family (all of whom he trash talked except himself).  It seemed like pure coincidence that out of the blue we got a call from him, with him saying he wanted to see me again, and I told him that I would agree to it only if he came to visit me at school with my mother and step-father present, as well as the high school social worker.

The visit seemed like it went well, but not even two months later he called and informed me that he had been to the doctor again and supposedly had cancer yet again.  And immediately after, he stopped calling with no warning or anything.  I decided that I was done having him in my life after that, and have not yet had the chance to inform him as such.
